abilities.name: Barrage

short: Ballistarii (Latin) - soldiers assigned as personnel to throwing machines, including ballistae. Their equipment probably consisted of a short spear and a small shield - illustrated in the Notitia Dignitatum. The crew that manned the ballista consisted of three members: one pointing man and his two assistants, who drew the charging mechanism (Amm., XXIII, 4,1). An experienced ballistarius could hit a target beyond the reach of arrows fired from a bow. Thus, during the siege of Amida, when the Chionitae king Grumbates and his retinue approached the walls to negotiate, his son was immediately killed by a shot from a ballista (Amm., XIX, 1,7). According to Zosimus, an arrow fired from a ballista could pierce two, three or more people at once (Zos., III, 21,2).
history: At close targets a 'ballista' could be aimed accurately, but at a cost in range; it could only fire around 500 metres. The machine used two torsion springs with levers inserted into twisted ropes made from animal sinew, giving incredible power for its size. Firing either solid shot or bolts, it was equally effective against infantry or cavalry, but could also be deployed to destroy light fortifications during sieges. Originally developed by the Greeks around 400BC, and based on the oversized 'oxybeles' composite bow, ballistae were widely used by many cultures of the period, including the Romans. Later Roman versions included adjustable caps that enabled crews to quickly alter the tension of each sinew bundle to provide balance and therefore improve accuracy.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
